# task-4ec00dd4: exterior markers fill hollow frame

Trigger: a thick rectangular outline (often color 5) surrounds an empty rectangular interior, with two isolated colored markers outside the frame.

## Observed rule
Fill the interior as a 2×2 checkerboard of solid quadrants using the two exterior marker colors. Preserve the outline, outside background, and marker cells.

For the demonstrated 10×10 frame, outline occupies rows 2–7 and columns 2–7; its 4×4 interior is rows 3–6, cols 3–6. Each quadrant is 2×2:
- top-left and bottom-right receive one marker color;
- top-right and bottom-left receive the other.

The ordering depends on the marker placement: observed markers both above the frame, left-to-right colors 4 then 8, yielded TL/BR=4 and TR/BL=8. Markers both below the frame, left-to-right colors 9 then 1, yielded TL/BR=1 and TR/BL=9 (reverse the left-to-right marker order). In other words, markers situated below the frame produced the opposite phase from markers above in the validated pair.

## Important caution
Do not simply put the left marker color in the top-left quadrant regardless of position. That was the first attempted rule and failed on the below-frame test. Infer frame/interior dimensions from the actual grid; keep markers and border unchanged.
